arm_resolution_note: Arms are curated per DONOR (AUT01-DN02, THY01-DN1, OVA01-DN278, ...); IEDB records per TISSUE (source_tissue takes 29 distinct values: Colon 7,389; Bladder 7,324; Skin 6,860; Aorta 5,742; ...) and never records which donor a peptide came from. The two axes are orthogonal, so no matcher can bridge them. 255,179 rows, the single largest block of arm-ambiguity in the corpus. title: HLA Ligand Atlas: a benign reference of HLA-presented peptides to improve T-cell-based cancer immunotherapy
note: 21 subjects (14 autopsy + 5 living thymus + 2 living ovary), 227 samples across 29 tissues (abstract says 227, Results section says 225 — likely 2 excluded after QC). Gold standard benign reference. None of the subjects was diagnosed with any malignant disease. Paired HLA-I (198 samples) and HLA-II (220 samples). Per-donor HLA from hla-ligand-atlas.org/rel/2020.12/donors.tsv.gz. Class II mhc entries include only DRB alleles (not DP/DQ) to match the DRB-only resolution in the IEDB mhc_restriction column for this PMID.

hla_alleles.class_i: 51 HLA-I allotypes (95% HLA-A, 74% HLA-B, 93% HLA-C population coverage)

arm_resolution_note: assay_comments carries 9 distinct statements and each one names the cell line and whether CIITA was induced, so it does vary WITH THE ARM rather than being study-level boilerplate; elution_condition_ids maps all 9 to their arms (#565). With the three parental class-II arms curated (#567), every statement now names exactly one arm per class except the three that name both conditions, and the rows left ambiguous are ambiguous BY EVIDENCE: their statement says the peptide was eluted from the parental and the CIITA sample alike, in whichever class it was found. That is 6,892 class-I rows and 330 class-II rows under the three paired statements. The 585 class-II rows under the parental-only statements (152 HROG02, 401 HROG17, 32 RA) now reach the parental arm they were eluted from. Before #567, 492 of them reached a CIITA-transduced arm on an allele typed in one line only -- provenance the deposit contradicts, which the exporter's statement veto refused -- and the remaining 93, on alleles shared between lines, reached no arm at all. Their arm carries the authors' own assessment that most are probable background; see the per-sample note. No general exclusion rule is derived from that assessment, here or anywhere else.
title: CIITA-Transduced Glioblastoma Cells Uncover a Rich Repertoire of Clinically Relevant Tumor-Associated HLA-II Antigens
note: 3 GBM cell lines (HROG02, HROG17, RA) profiled as parental (CIITA-) and CIITA-transduced (CIITA+). GBM cells do not naturally express HLA-II, so the class-II repertoire this paper reports comes from forced CIITA expression. Parental class I data is unperturbed. The parental lines were nonetheless run through the HLA-II affinity plate as well and yielded class-II identifications — 165, 651 and 83 peptides — which the authors read as mostly background contaminants; those arms are curated with that assessment attached rather than dropped (#567).
perturbations: CIITA transduction (flag-CIITA plasmid, G418 selection) — forces HLA-II expression on GBM

ms_samples.note: This arm's HLA-II repertoire is the one the transduction produced. It also receives the peptides whose deposited statement names both the parental and the CIITA-treated condition, rather than leaving those ambiguous between the two class-II arms, because the paper establishes HLA-II presentation only after transduction ("While HROG02, HROG17, and RA cells express HLA-I, they do not express HLA-DR, HLA-DP, and HLA-DQ molecules (supplemental Fig. S1)") and reads the parental class-II identifications as background ("suggesting that a background level of potential contaminants contributed to these identifications"). Co-detection in the parental sample is a property of those particular peptides and is recoverable from their own assay_comments; it is not evidence of parental presentation, and it says nothing about the rest of this arm's peptides. Class I is treated the other way round on the same statements: both conditions do present class I, so a class-I peptide named under both stays ambiguous between them. The asymmetry between the two classes is the biology the paper reports, not a curation shortcut -- the parental cells present class I and do not present class II.

title: HLA-DP peptidome promiscuity across immunogenicity groups
note: HLA-DP class II. IEDB "Bone Marrow" likely refers to transplant donor context, not tissue source. Cell lines used.

study_label: Nanaware 2019 — HLA-DO KO mouse class II
arm_resolution_note: The two curated arms differ only by HLA-DO genotype (mouse splenocytes WT against mouse splenocytes DO KO), and no deposited field records DO status: antigen_processing_comments and assay_comments are both absent (0 distinct values). What does vary is the sample system. cell_name and source_tissue take 2 values each and split the same way, B cell / Blood 6,912 against Splenocyte / Spleen 757, tracking mhc_restriction's split of human HLA-DRA*01:01/DRB1*01:01 (6,912) against mouse H2-AA*b/AB*b (757). That axis is orthogonal to the curated one: both arms are mouse splenocytes typed H-2Ab, so the 757 mouse rows cannot be divided between WT and knockout, and the 6,912 human DR1-restricted rows sit in a system the arms do not cover. Curating a human DR1 arm would still leave the DO-positive against DO-null distinction unrecorded on every row.
